I have been picking up needles and syringes at this surgery for years to do my B12 injections at home. In total, I have been administering my own B12 injections for nearly 15 years. However, 2 days ago after an appointment, I asked at the desk if the nurse was available to give me some more (she usually gives me 3 at a time) and the receptionist said the nurse couldn't do that. I explained that this had been routine for years and she said someone would call me. I received a call today saying a Dr. Toby, who I have never seen, said that I wasn't allowed to do my injections myself and had to come to the surgery due to "self injurious" behaviour LAST YEAR. My "self injurious" behaviour was feeling suicidal due to ongoing domestic abuse, which has since been resolved. I am adult who lives by myself with access to professional kitchen knives and enough opiate and benzo medications to sedate a donkey, yet this doctor who knows absolutely nothing about me nor my situation has decided that I am no longer allowed to do something that I've been safely doing for 15 years. Getting to the surgery as a disabled person who often relies on a wheelchair and doesn't drive is a massive inconvenience when I can simply do my injections at home.

I have been in ongoing, severe pain for over two weeks and have been back and forth between the hospital and this practice with no resolution. During this time, I have been seen by four different doctors for the same issue, each insisting on a same-day assessment rather than reviewing previous notes, only to then refer me elsewhere. This has been incredibly frustrating, particularly as I work full-time and do not receive paid sick leave or paid time off for medical appointments. I have explained this repeatedly, yet I continue to be asked to attend frequent in-person assessments with no progress.

Today I was asked to attend yet another appointment at 4:15pm. I allowed extra time to travel from work due to traffic, and at 4:10pm I phoned reception to explain that I was on my way and might be a couple of minutes late due to school traffic. I was told this was fine and that there was a 10-minute grace period before the doctor may not see me.

I arrived at 4:19pm and attempted to check in using the electronic screen, as I usually do. The screen instructed me to check in at reception. Both receptionists were on the phones and laptops and did not look up or acknowledge me. I stood at the desk, moving between both sides, for approximately nine minutes trying to be seen, making direct eye contact, but was ignored.

Before the 10-minute grace period had even passed, I saw my doctor’s name flash up calling the next patient. Only then did a receptionist speak to me and tell me that I had “wasted time” by attempting to check in on the screen and that I should have checked in at reception immediately. I explained that I followed the on-screen instructions and had been standing there waiting to be acknowledged, but the receptionist repeatedly talked over me, dismissed what I was saying, and insisted that I was at fault.

Despite explaining that the doctor called the next patient before the grace period had ended and that both receptionists had been occupied the entire time, I was spoken to in a rude and condescending manner. I was then told I could sit and wait while the doctor decided whether she wanted to see me or not.

At this point, after weeks of unresolved pain and feeling completely unheard, I left the practice. The way I was spoken to and treated was unacceptable. The behaviour displayed by the receptionist was unprofessional, dismissive, and entirely inappropriate for a front-facing role — especially when dealing with a 19-year-old patient who is clearly unwell and in significant pain.

This practice needs to seriously review how patients are communicated with and how vulnerable individuals are treated.
